slices.title: Add the three 18.20.0 host segments to SYSTEM_TEMPLATE.md
slices.done_when: With SRC naming a directory whose omp-config child is the PR checkout and @oh-my-pi/* at the PR-time release, `bun /tmp/omp-template-render.ts` prints {"editCritical":true,"shapeNotice":true,"readUrlsPointer":true,"editCriticalOff":false,"shapeNoticeOff":false,"readUrlsPointerOff":false} and exits 0, where the baseline commit prints the first three readings false (verified in /tmp: baseline {"editCritical":false,"shapeNotice":false,"readUrlsPointer":false,…}).

slices.title: Widen the xd:// device rule to both backtick spellings
slices.done_when: With OMOMP_MODE unset (full mode) `bun /tmp/omp-device-rule.ts` prints {"devicesEdits":2,"toolRefCaptured":true,"userReportedReplaced":true,"compiledCodeReplaced":true,"evalFileRuleApplied":true} and exits 0, where the baseline prints devicesEdits:1 and exits 1 (both readings reproduced in /tmp from a copy of agent/: baseline 1, candidate regex `… to \`?xd://<tool>\`? via \`([^`]+)\`\.` 2).

slices.title: Prove the prompt segments and the device rule in real sandbox sessions
slices.done_when: In one `bun sandbox/sandbox.ts hold --repo <PR checkout>` whose container `omp --version` prints the PR-time release, a default-config session's newest /tmp/omp-llm-request-*.json gives `grep -c` 1 for each of `File edits: MUST use`, `Further sub-paths, queries, limits: xd://read/urls`, `Devices are not functions`, `# Code by Syntax Shape` and `§ Delivery`, and after the four added `spotlight.experiment.enabled: true` / `encourageEdits: false` lines the second session's newest dump gives 1 for `Long results are shaped:`, 0 for `File edits: MUST use`, and 1 for `xd://read/urls`.

slices.title: Repo hygiene gates on the combined change
slices.done_when: `bun run check`, `bun run test`, and `bun ci/check.ts` in a throwaway HOME (exit 0; exit 2 only when the free model is unavailable, requiring a rerun) all pass on the PR checkout, and `grep -rn "Long results are shaped" agent` prints nothing.

open_points.point: Every rule in the shipped rule file carries mode: "full", so under OMOMP_MODE=light no rule applies at all: the device sentence renders unreplaced in `omp-light`, and the function scripts' rows 1-4 readings depend on the caller's mode, which the acceptance table's Env column never names. Result 4 states the two-spelling match without a mode condition.
open_points.input: `OMOMP_MODE=light SRC=<dir containing omp-config> bun /tmp/omp-device-rule.ts` (equivalently, running it from an omp-light session's shell, which inherits the variable), and `/dump` in an `omp-light` session.
outputs: {"devicesEdits":2,"toolRefCaptured":true,"userReportedReplaced":true,"compiledCodeReplaced":true,"evalFileRuleApplied":true} with exit 0 — row 4's stated expectation, since nothing conditions the rule on mode

{"devicesEdits":0,"toolRefCaptured":false,"userReportedReplaced":false,"compiledCodeReplaced":false,"evalFileRuleApplied":false} with exit 1, and an unchanged `# xd:// Tool Devices` line in the light session — what happens today, because agent/extensions/_shared/prompt-conditions.ts:147 derives the mode from OMOMP_MODE and all seven rules of agent/extensions-last/system-prompt-replace/REPLACE-SYSTEM-default.yml set mode: "full"
open_points.producer: agent/omp-light.ts:57 spawns omp with env { ...process.env, OMOMP_MODE: "light" }, and every tool shell of that session inherits it; agent/extensions/_shared/prompt-conditions.ts:147 reads it.
open_points.searched: grep -rn OMOMP_MODE over the checkout (agent/omp-light.ts, agent/extensions/_shared/prompt-conditions.ts, docs/operations.md, docs/plugins-and-modes.md); ran /tmp/omp-device-rule.ts at the baseline commit with OMOMP_MODE=light (all readings false, exit 1) and with `env -u OMOMP_MODE` (devicesEdits 1, matching the contract's baseline reading).

open_points.point: Both acceptance scripts resolve the checkout as join(SRC, "omp-config") (and Bun.resolveSync from there), but the acceptance table's Env column only says "PR 分支检出", so a PR checkout whose directory is not named omp-config — a delivery worktree or a harness checkout such as .../oh-my-omp-omp-config-323/base — cannot be named by SRC.
open_points.input: `SRC=/tmp/delivering-issues bun /tmp/omp-template-render.ts` where the PR checkout is /tmp/delivering-issues/oh-my-omp-omp-config-323/base.
outputs: the rows 1-4 readings and exit 0 — nothing in the contract constrains the checkout's directory name

ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/delivering-issues/omp-config/agent/SYSTEM_TEMPLATE.md' inside the script, before any reading — what happens today (reproduced), and the same failure for the second script's import of agent/extensions-last/system-prompt-replace/index.ts
open_points.producer: none in the repository: sandbox/sandbox.ts:73 takes `--repo DIR` and defaults to the checkout containing sandbox/, ci/check.ts:30 resolves REPO from import.meta.dir, and no file under .omp/commands/ or docs/*.md fixes a checkout name; the input comes from the harness that materialized this checkout as .../base.
open_points.searched: grep -rn "worktree" and "--repo"/REPO over sandbox/, ci/, .omp/commands/ and docs/; ran both scripts with SRC naming the parent of a checkout called `base` (ENOENT) and of a symlink named omp-config (readings produced).

open_points.point: Rows 5 and 6 leave `<模型>` unresolved, and the sandbox deletes the credentials of every provider without a recorder target, so the two request dumps exist only for a model whose provider declares a baseUrl; with any other model the greps read no file. The contract states neither which model to use nor what the rows mean when the dump is absent.
open_points.input: `docker exec -it -w /work omp-sandbox-<run> omp --model <provider>/<model>` where <provider> has no baseUrl in the container's copied models.yml, followed by `/dump`.
outputs: the counts 1/1/1/1/1 of row 5 and 1/0/1 of row 6 — the table's Expect column, which presumes a credentialed model

no /tmp/omp-llm-request-*.json at all, so `ls -t /tmp/omp-llm-request-*.json | head -1` is empty and each `grep -c … "$f"` fails or reads an empty path — what the sandbox records as untested for such a provider
open_points.producer: sandbox/recorder.ts:124 deletes every auth_credentials row whose provider is not in the recorder's provider list, re-checked at sandbox/recorder.ts:131; sandbox/recorder.ts:117-131 works from the baseUrl rewrite that only providers declaring a baseUrl receive (sandbox/README.md:50).
open_points.searched: read sandbox/README.md §Credentials and the recorder description; grep auth_credentials/baseUrl over sandbox/*.ts; confirmed host-side that bare `/dump` writes the sidecar (pi-coding-agent src/modes/controllers/command-controller.ts:411 → src/session/agent-session.ts:16129), so the file exists exactly when a credentialed request happened.

gate_gaps.row: 结果 1 / 验收 #1: `encourageEdits` 开掉或没有 `edit` 时这一段不出现 (the `{{#has tools "edit"}}` guard)
gate_gaps.input: A render with `encourageEdits: true` and `tools` holding read/write/grep/find/task/bash/eval/todo but NOT `edit` (row 1's `off` case turns `encourageEdits` off as well, and row 6 does so in a real session); verified in /tmp that this input renders no `File edits:` line, so the guard is expressible and no acceptance row feeds it.

gate_gaps.row: 结果 1 / 验收 #1: bash/eval 在场时带 sed/perl 子句 (the `{{#ifAny (includes tools "bash") (includes tools "eval")}}` branch)
gate_gaps.input: A render with `encourageEdits: true` and `edit` present but neither `bash` nor `eval` in `tools`; verified in /tmp that this input yields exactly `File edits: MUST use \`edit\`.` with no sed/perl clause — no acceptance row feeds the false branch of that `ifAny`.

gate_gaps.row: 结果 2 / 验收 #2: resultShaping “在 `# Tool I/O` 下渲染”
gate_gaps.input: A template that renders `{{resultShaping}}` under any other heading (e.g. after `# Delegation`): rows 1-2 only call `String.includes("SHAPE-NOTICE")`, and rows 5-6 only `grep -c` the phrase in a JSON dump where the whole system prompt is one line, so placement is never observed — extracting the text from `# Tool I/O` to the next heading would.

gate_gaps.row: 结果 3 / 验收 #3: “`# Internal URLs` 首行带 `Further sub-paths, queries, limits: xd://read/urls.`”
gate_gaps.input: A template that places the pointer as the last line of the `internalUrls` list instead of the heading's first line: `readUrlsPointer` and row 5's `grep -c` both still pass, so first-line placement is unobserved — asserting the line following `# Internal URLs` would observe it.

gate_gaps.row: 结果 5 [保持] / 验收 #5: “模板的 `§` 标记、`# Code by Syntax Shape`、`Topics` 段与 Delegation/Workflow/Delivery 段落照旧渲染”
gate_gaps.input: A template edit that drops `# Delegation`, the tool-topics `Topics` paragraph, or the `§ Workflow` marker while keeping `# Code by Syntax Shape` and `§ Delivery`: every acceptance row still passes (row 5 greps only those two strings; rows 1-3 assert nothing about preserved sections).

gate_gaps.row: 决策表「设备规则的匹配形式」: 一条同时接受两种写法的正则 (被否方案是“两种写法各写一条规则”)
gate_gaps.input: A rule file carrying two spelling-specific rules instead of one tolerant rule: verified in /tmp that this variant yields the identical row-4 reading {"devicesEdits":2,"toolRefCaptured":true,…} with exit 0, because the synthetic prompt holds one line of each spelling — so the reading cannot distinguish the decision; only an assertion on the file itself (one `Write JSON args as \`content\` to \`?xd://` rule) observes it.

gate_gaps.row: 决策表「设备规则的匹配形式」: “模板行保持现状” (the repo template keeps its backticked `Write JSON args as \`content\` to \`xd://<tool>\` via \`{{toolRefs.write}}\`.` line)
gate_gaps.input: A PR that instead aligns agent/SYSTEM_TEMPLATE.md:86 to the bundled no-backtick spelling: rows 4-6 still pass (the script's prompt is hard-coded with both spellings and row 5's grep is spelling-independent), and rows 1-3 do not read that line at all — asserting the template's device line (or the render output) would observe the decision.
